title: Reading the readouts without looking away
target: Which readout in R.E.P.O. answers which question, so the screen is read rather than stared at.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A crew to keep track of

steps.do: Know which readout answers which question rather than scanning all of them.
steps.because: health, the haul, the goal and item details each have a readout of their own under one state readout (HUD, HealthUI, HaulUI, GoalUI, ItemInfoUI)

steps.do: Look for the second item readout when the first one is not enough.
steps.because: item details have a second readout for extra information (ItemInfoExtraUI)

steps.do: Use the value screen to price what is in front of you.
steps.because: what something is worth has its own screen element (ValueScreen)

steps.do: Check the shop's own readouts between runs instead of guessing what it costs.
steps.because: the shop has readouts for what it costs and how it is growing (ShopCostUI, ShopIncreaseUI)

steps.do: Read the level and run readouts before you commit to a plan.
steps.because: there are readouts for the level and for the run record (LevelUI, StatsUI)

steps.do: Read the numbers that float over things, not only the fixed readout.
steps.because: the floating value text has intro and outro curves, a colour and a text size for a value and another pair for a cost (WorldSpaceUIValue, curveIntro, curveOutro, colorValue, colorCost, textSizeValue, textSizeCost)

steps.do: Notice when value is lost, because it has an object of its own.
steps.because: there is a world-space interface parent and a separate object for value that has been lost (WorldSpaceUIParent, WorldSpaceUIValueLost)

steps.do: Learn the discovery graphic's three colour pairs so the news is read at a glance.
steps.because: the graphic has a colour pair for a discovery, one for a reminder and one for bad news, each with a corner and a middle colour, and it can be anchored to the middle or to any corner (ValuableDiscoverGraphic, colorDiscoverCorner, colorDiscoverMiddle, ColorReminderCorner, ColorBadCorner, middle, topLeft, topRight, botLeft, botRight)

commonMistakes: Watching the readout you always watch while the haul readout is the one changing.
Missing the second line of item detail and guessing what the item does.
Reading a floating number as a value when it was a cost.
Treating every coloured flash as good news.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
